provinces.stateName: Archipiélago de San Andrés, Providencia y Santa Catalina

states.name: Archipiélago de San Andrés, Providencia y Santa Catalina

nations.name: Abu Dhabi
nations.eraSummary: The Trucial coast lives on pearls and lives with the British maritime truce that ended the Gulf's own naval wars.

nations.name: Afghanistan
nations.eraSummary: Afghanistan is divided between Dost Mohammad in Kabul and rivals in Kandahar and Herat. Peshawar has been lost to the Sikhs.

nations.name: Algeria
nations.eraSummary: The Regency of Algiers answers to Constantinople only nominally. A French fleet is already being fitted out.

nations.name: Argentina
nations.eraSummary: The provinces of the Rio de la Plata are a confederation in name. Rosas has just taken Buenos Aires.

nations.name: Atjeh
nations.eraSummary: The sultanate of Aceh trades pepper on its own terms, guaranteed for now by the Anglo-Dutch treaty that drew a line down the Malacca strait.

nations.name: Beroda
nations.eraSummary: Berar is held under the same subsidiary terms that follow every Maratha defeat.

nations.name: Bolivia
nations.eraSummary: Bolivia carries Sucre's constitution and Bolivar's name, and has just lost both men.

nations.name: Brazil
nations.eraSummary: Pedro I's empire is intact but his position is not. He will abdicate next year and leave a five year old on the throne.

nations.name: Brunei
nations.eraSummary: Brunei's sultan claims the north Borneo coast and controls rather less of it than he claims.

nations.name: Bukkhara
nations.eraSummary: The emirate of Bukhara is the religious centre of Central Asia and a slave market that Russia will later cite as a reason to arrive.

nations.name: Burma
nations.eraSummary: Burma is five years past the treaty of Yandabo, which cost it Arakan, Assam and Tenasserim and put a British Resident in Ava.

nations.name: Cambodia
nations.eraSummary: Cambodia is held down by Vietnam and claimed by Siam. Minh Mang's officials are reorganising the country as a Vietnamese province.

nations.name: Chile
nations.eraSummary: Chile has just ended its civil war at Lircay. The conservative republic Portales is building will outlast almost every government on the continent.

nations.name: New Granada
nations.eraSummary: Gran Colombia is breaking apart. Bolivar has resigned, Venezuela and Ecuador are leaving, and he will be dead by December.

nations.name: Denmark
nations.eraSummary: Frederick VI governs Denmark, Norway lost, and the German duchies of Schleswig and Holstein held on terms nobody has yet been forced to define.

nations.name: Egypt
nations.eraSummary: Muhammad Ali rules Egypt as an Ottoman viceroy in name and an independent power in fact. Syria is next.

nations.name: United Kingdom
nations.eraSummary: The workshop of the world and the first industrial society. Catholic emancipation passed last year, the Reform crisis is a year away, and the Company governs India in the Crown's name.

nations.name: Spain
nations.eraSummary: Ferdinand VII has no son and has just set aside the Salic law for his unborn child. The American empire is gone, and the Carlist question is being created in the palace.

nations.name: Ethiopia
nations.eraSummary: The Zemene Mesafint: the emperor at Gondar reigns, and the regional rases rule.

nations.name: Grand Duchy of Finland
nations.eraSummary: The Tsar rules as Grand Duke through the Senate in Helsinki. Finland keeps Swedish law, its own customs frontier and no Diet: none has been convened since 1809.

nations.name: France
nations.eraSummary: Charles X governs through ministers the Chamber will not accept. An expedition against Algiers is fitting out, and the July Revolution is six months away.

nations.name: Kingdom of Greece
nations.eraSummary: The London Protocol of February 1830 makes Greek independence a fact of European law.

nations.name: Haiti
nations.eraSummary: Boyer governs the whole of Hispaniola and pays France for the recognition of a freedom Haiti won for itself.

nations.name: Hawaii
nations.eraSummary: Kamehameha III rules a kingdom unified barely a generation ago. The sandalwood forests are nearly cut out and the whalers have found Honolulu.

nations.name: Hesse-Kassel
nations.eraSummary: The Electorate of Hesse-Kassel is a small German state with an unpopular prince. The unrest of this autumn will win it a constitution in January.

nations.name: Holstein
nations.eraSummary: The duchies of Schleswig and Holstein answer to the Danish king, though Holstein is also a member of the German Confederation.

nations.name: Hyderabad
nations.eraSummary: The Nizam keeps his throne and his court, and the Company keeps a subsidiary army in Hyderabad.

nations.name: Johore
nations.eraSummary: Johor and its Riau islands are split by that same treaty, the sultanate divided between British and Dutch spheres.

nations.name: Tokugawa Shogunate
nations.eraSummary: The Tokugawa keep the country closed. The outside world reaches Japan through one Dutch factory in Nagasaki harbour.

nations.name: Kalat
nations.eraSummary: The khan of Kalat holds the Baluch confederacy together loosely, between Sindh, Persia and Kabul.

nations.name: Khiva
nations.eraSummary: The khanate of Khiva raids the Turkmen steppe and the Russian caravan routes, which is the pretext Russia is waiting for.

nations.name: Kokand
nations.eraSummary: Kokand controls the Ferghana valley and the trade over the passes into Kashgar.

nations.name: Joseon Korea
nations.eraSummary: Joseon Korea trades with Qing China and tolerates a Japanese post at Pusan. Catholic converts are persecuted.

nations.name: Liberia
nations.eraSummary: Liberia is a settlement of freed American slaves on land bought by a colonisation society, not yet a state.

nations.name: Madagascar
nations.eraSummary: Ranavalona I rules Madagascar and has begun turning the missionaries and their treaties back out to sea.

nations.name: Mexico
nations.eraSummary: Mexico is nine years independent and already cycling through governments. Texas is filling with American settlers the government cannot count.

nations.name: Mongolia
nations.eraSummary: The Mongol banners are administered directly from Peking.

nations.name: Moldavia
nations.eraSummary: Moldavia is an Ottoman tributary under Russian occupation, governed by the Reglement Organique that Russia wrote for it last year.

nations.name: Morocco
nations.eraSummary: The sultan of Morocco governs the coast directly and the mountains by negotiation. The French landing at Algiers will change what its eastern border means.

nations.name: Mysore
nations.eraSummary: Mysore is under Company administration this year, its raja set aside after the Nagar rebellion.

nations.name: Nagpur
nations.eraSummary: The Bhonsle raja of Nagpur rules under a subsidiary alliance, his army capped and his foreign policy the Company's.

nations.name: Nejd
nations.eraSummary: The Al Saud have retaken Riyadh and are rebuilding the emirate that Egypt destroyed in 1818.

nations.name: Nepal
nations.eraSummary: Nepal is bound by the treaty of Sugauli, its borders fixed and a British Resident in Kathmandu.

nations.name: Netherlands
nations.eraSummary: William I rules the United Kingdom of the Netherlands from The Hague. The southern provinces resent the Dutch language, the Dutch debt and the Dutch church, and are eight months from revolt.

nations.name: Oman
nations.eraSummary: Said bin Sultan rules from Muscat and increasingly from Zanzibar, holding the cloves, the slaves and the ivory of the East African trade.

nations.name: Ottoman Empire
nations.eraSummary: Greece is lost and Serbian autonomy conceded. Mahmud II destroyed the janissaries in 1826 and is building a new army from nothing while Muhammad Ali watches from Cairo.

nations.name: Panjab
nations.eraSummary: The Sikh empire under Ranjit Singh is the last independent power of any size in India, with an army drilled by European officers.

nations.name: Papal States
nations.eraSummary: The Papal States are governed by cardinals and policed by Austria. The Legations have rebelled before and will again.

nations.name: Persia
nations.eraSummary: Qajar Persia lost the Caucasus to Russia at Turkmanchay two years ago, along with the right to keep a fleet on the Caspian.

nations.name: Peru
nations.eraSummary: Peru is independent, indebted and governed by whichever general holds Lima.

nations.name: Kingdom of Poland
nations.eraSummary: Congress Poland still has its own sejm, army and constitution. The November Uprising is ten months away.

nations.name: Portugal
nations.eraSummary: Miguel holds Lisbon as an absolutist usurper while his brother Pedro rules Brazil. The civil war between them is coming.

nations.name: Paraguay
nations.eraSummary: Francia rules Paraguay in isolation, with the rivers closed and the country fed by its own farms.

nations.name: Qing Empire
nations.eraSummary: The Qing govern roughly a third of humanity and treat foreign trade as a privilege granted at Canton. The silver balance of the opium trade has just begun to run the wrong way.

nations.name: Russian Empire
nations.eraSummary: Nicholas I rules on Orthodoxy, autocracy and nationality. The Turkish war ended last year at Adrianople, and Poland keeps its own army and constitution for ten more months.

nations.name: Sardinia-Piedmont
nations.eraSummary: Sardinia-Piedmont is the only Italian state with an army worth the name, which is why every plan for Italy eventually arrives at its door.

nations.name: Serbia
nations.eraSummary: The hatt-i sharif of 1830 confirms Serbian autonomy under Ottoman suzerainty.

nations.name: Siam
nations.eraSummary: Rama III rules from Bangkok, pressing claims into Laos and Cambodia while Britain consolidates in Burma.

nations.name: Sindh
nations.eraSummary: The Talpur amirs rule Sindh from Hyderabad and Khairpur, watching the Company move up the Indus.

nations.name: Sokoto
nations.eraSummary: The Sokoto caliphate is the largest state in West Africa, run from Sokoto and Gwandu since Usman dan Fodio's jihad.

nations.name: Sweden
nations.eraSummary: Bernadotte, once a marshal of Napoleon, rules Sweden and Norway in personal union. The two kingdoms share a king and almost nothing else.

nations.name: Switzerland
nations.eraSummary: The Confederation is a league of sovereign cantons under the 1815 pact. The liberal Regeneration is beginning in the cantonal assemblies, not in Bern.

nations.name: Tibet
nations.eraSummary: Lhasa governs itself under the watch of the Qing ambans.

nations.name: Travancore
nations.eraSummary: Travancore is a subsidiary ally on the Malabar coast, with a Resident at the court and a Company garrison.

nations.name: Tripoli
nations.eraSummary: Karamanli Tripoli is in its last years of autonomy before direct Ottoman rule returns.

nations.name: Two Sicilies
nations.eraSummary: The Two Sicilies are ruled from Naples by a Bourbon restored twice by Austrian bayonets.

nations.name: Tunis
nations.eraSummary: The Husainid beys govern Tunis as hereditary Ottoman vassals.

nations.name: The USCA
nations.eraSummary: The Federal Republic of Central America is held together by Morazan and very little else.

nations.name: Uruguay
nations.eraSummary: Uruguay is three years old, created as a buffer so that Brazil and Argentina would stop fighting over it. Its first constitution is sworn this year.

nations.name: United States
nations.eraSummary: Twenty four states and Jackson in his first term. The Indian Removal Act passed this year, and cotton is moving west faster than Congress can organise territory for it.

nations.name: Dai Nam
nations.eraSummary: Minh Mang rules a Vietnam recently unified, centralising the administration on a Chinese model and closing it to missionaries.

nations.name: Wallachia
nations.eraSummary: Wallachia, like Moldavia, is Ottoman in law and Russian in practice, with a boyar assembly and a Russian protector.

nations.name: Xinjiang
nations.eraSummary: Xinjiang is held by Qing garrisons and an uneasy peace with the Khojas.

nations.name: Yemen
nations.eraSummary: The imams of Sanaa hold the highlands. The coffee trade of Mocha has passed its peak.

nations.name: Zulu
nations.eraSummary: Dingane rules the Zulu kingdom after Shaka's assassination two years ago.

nations.name: Kazakh Hordes
nations.flagNote: existing game design, a stylised steppe emblem rather than a documented 1830 flag
nations.eraSummary: Russia abolished the khans of the Middle Horde in 1822 and the Junior Horde in 1824, and the steppe is now run by sultans and clan elders. The Senior Horde to the south pays court to Kokand and the Qing.

nations.name: Rajput States
nations.eraSummary: The treaties of 1817 and 1818 bound Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur and the other Rajput courts to the East India Company. The princes keep their thrones and their quarrels, and the Company keeps the peace between them.

nations.name: Bornu
nations.eraSummary: Muhammad al-Amin al-Kanemi governs Bornu from Kukawa, the town he founded in 1814, while the Sayfawa mai keeps the throne in name. He has held the Sokoto jihad at bay for two decades.

nations.name: Massina
nations.eraSummary: Seku Amadu's Fulani caliphate rules the inner Niger delta from Hamdullahi, the capital he founded in 1820. Its councils enforce strict Maliki law, and Timbuktu has acknowledged its authority since 1826.

nations.name: Banjar
nations.eraSummary: Sultan Adam rules Banjar from Martapura. The contract of 1826 handed most of southeastern Borneo to the Dutch and leaves the sultanate a dependency of Batavia.

nations.name: Darfur
nations.flagNote: existing game design, stylised; Darfur used banners but no single documented state flag
nations.eraSummary: Sultan Muhammad al-Fadl rules from El Fasher. Darfur lost Kordofan to Muhammad Ali's army in 1821 and still sends caravans down the Forty Days Road to Egypt.

nations.name: Asante
nations.flagNote: existing game design built on the Golden Stool emblem; Asante had no national flag in 1830
nations.eraSummary: Asantehene Osei Yaw Akoto rules from Kumasi over the gold and kola trade of the forest. The defeat at Katamanso in 1826 broke Asante's hold on the coast, and peace with the British forts has not yet been signed.

nations.name: Wadai
nations.eraSummary: Wadai rules from Wara and holds Bagirmi as a tributary. The caravan road north to Benghazi, opened under Sultan Sabun, carries its ivory and slaves.

nations.name: Rwanda
nations.eraSummary: Mwami Yuhi IV Gahindiro rules the highland kingdom through cattle chiefs and army lineages. The court moves between royal residences rather than keeping a fixed capital.

nations.name: Comanche
nations.eraSummary: Comanche bands hold the southern plains between the Arkansas and the Texas frontier. They trade horses and captives across the region and raid deep into northern Mexico.

nations.name: Burundi
nations.eraSummary: Mwami Ntare IV Rugamba has spent three decades enlarging Burundi to the east and north. Princes of the royal line govern the provinces under him.

nations.name: Majeerteen
nations.eraSummary: The Majeerteen sultan rules the northeastern Horn from Bargal. Frankincense, gums and the salvage of wrecks on the Guardafui coast pay for his court.

nations.name: Mahra
nations.eraSummary: The Afrar sultans of Mahra rule the coast around Qishn and the island of Socotra. Their subjects keep their own South Arabian language.

nations.name: Luang Phrabang
nations.eraSummary: King Manthaturath rules Luang Phrabang as a tributary of Bangkok. Siam crushed Vientiane in 1828, and Luang Phrabang is the last Lao court on the Mekong with its own king.

nations.name: Ngoyo
nations.eraSummary: The Mangoyo rules the coast around Cabinda. Its harbour is one of the busiest slaving ports north of the Congo, frequented by Portuguese and Brazilian ships.

nations.name: Futa Toro
nations.eraSummary: Futa Toro is a Muslim imamate on the middle Senegal. Its almamy is elected by Torodbe clerics who hold the real power, and the river trade with Saint-Louis pays tolls to them.

nations.name: Oyo
nations.eraSummary: The Oyo empire is breaking apart. Ilorin has passed to emirs allied with Sokoto, Dahomey no longer pays tribute, and the Alaafin's capital at Oyo-Ile is under threat.

nations.name: Riau-Lingga
nations.eraSummary: The treaty of 1824 cut the old Johor realm in two. The sultan at Daik on Lingga is under Dutch protection, and Bugis viceroys govern from Penyengat.

nations.name: Kakongo
nations.eraSummary: Kakongo's king rules from Kinguele, and its port of Malemba trades slaves and ivory with European ships off the Loango coast.

nations.name: Sulu
nations.eraSummary: Sultan Jamalul Kiram I rules from Jolo. Sulu's prosperity rests on trade with China and on Iranun and Balangingi raiders who take captives across the Spanish Philippines.

nations.name: Chiang Mai
nations.eraSummary: The Chet Ton princes rule Chiang Mai and the Lanna principalities as tributaries of Bangkok. They repopulated the north with war captives after the Burmese were driven out.

nations.name: Awadh
nations.flagNote: existing game design built on the twin-fish emblem of the Awadh court
nations.eraSummary: King Nasir-ud-Din Haidar rules at Lucknow under a Company resident. Awadh ceded half its territory to the Company in 1801 and keeps a lavish court on the rest.

nations.name: Bhutan
nations.flagNote: existing game design in the later yellow and orange dragon pattern
nations.eraSummary: Bhutan is governed by a civil ruler, the Druk Desi, beside the Je Khenpo of the Drukpa church. The regional governors of Paro and Tongsa are steadily gaining power at his expense.

nations.name: Shoshone
nations.eraSummary: Eastern and Northern Shoshone bands range from the Wind River to the Snake. American and British trappers hold their summer rendezvous in Shoshone country.

nations.name: Niani
nations.eraSummary: Niani is a Mandinka kingdom on the north bank of the middle Gambia. British traders from Bathurst buy hides and beeswax at its river landings.

nations.name: Jolof
nations.eraSummary: The Buurba Jolof once held the overlordship of all the Wolof kingdoms. Jolof is now an inland state of herders, overshadowed by Kajoor and Waalo on the coast.

nations.name: Dahomey
nations.eraSummary: King Gezo rules from Abomey. He has stopped paying tribute to Oyo, and his army, with its corps of women soldiers, raids for the coastal slave trade at Ouidah.

nations.name: Waalo
nations.eraSummary: The Brak of Waalo rules the lower Senegal next to Saint-Louis. A French plantation scheme on Waalo land is failing, and Trarza raiders press from the north bank.

nations.name: Bundu
nations.eraSummary: The Sissibe almamys rule Bundu, a Muslim Fulbe state between the upper Senegal and the Gambia. It trades gum and gold with the French post at Bakel.

nations.name: Wuli
nations.eraSummary: Wuli is a Mandinka kingdom on the upper Gambia, ruled by its mansa from Medina. Caravans to the coast pay it tolls.

nations.name: Maguindanao
nations.eraSummary: The Maguindanao sultan rules the Pulangi valley and the Illana coast from Cotabato. Spain claims Mindanao but holds only a few forts on it.

nations.name: Bahawalpur
nations.eraSummary: Nawab Bahawal Khan III of the Daudpotra dynasty rules the desert state along the Sutlej. Ranjit Singh's Sikhs press from the north and Sindh from the south.

nations.name: Saloum
nations.eraSummary: The Buur Saloum rules from Kahone. The kingdom's wealth is salt from the Saloum estuary, traded inland for cattle and cloth.

nations.name: Haushabi
nations.eraSummary: The Haushabi sultans hold a small tribal territory north of Lahej, astride the road from Aden to the highlands.

nations.name: Dine
nations.eraSummary: Navajo bands hold the canyon and mesa country west of the Rio Grande. They herd sheep and horses and alternate trade and raiding with Mexican New Mexico.

nations.name: Jambi
nations.eraSummary: The sultan of Jambi rules the Batang Hari basin of central Sumatra. Pepper and forest goods go downriver, and the Dutch have not yet forced a treaty on the court.

nations.name: Manipur
nations.eraSummary: Raja Gambhir Singh restored Manipur in 1826 with British help after seven years of Burmese occupation. The Treaty of Yandabo recognised the kingdom's independence.

nations.name: Perak
nations.eraSummary: Perak's sultans rule the tin country of the western peninsula. The Anglo-Siamese treaty of 1826 ended Siamese claims on Perak, and Penang watches its affairs closely.

nations.name: Shilluk
nations.eraSummary: The reth of the Shilluk rules from Fashoda over a dense chain of villages along the White Nile. Egyptian Sudan lies to the north and has not yet reached him.

nations.name: Kajoor
nations.eraSummary: The Damel of Kajoor rules the Wolof coast between Saint-Louis and Cape Verde. His ceddo warriors and the kingdom's Muslim clerics are in long rivalry.

nations.name: Mecklenburg-Schwerin
nations.eraSummary: Grand Duke Friedrich Franz I holds court at Ludwigslust. Mecklenburg is governed under the estates settlement of 1755, and its knights hold the land and the peasants who work it.

nations.name: Sambaliung
nations.eraSummary: Sambaliung is one of the two sultanates formed when Berau split in east Borneo. It trades birds' nests and forest goods with Bugis and Sulu merchants.

nations.name: Lahej
nations.eraSummary: The Abdali sultans rule Lahej and the port of Aden, a small town in decline since the Mocha coffee trade moved on. British ships call there for water.

nations.name: Kutai
nations.eraSummary: Sultan Muhammad Salehuddin rules Kutai from Tenggarong on the Mahakam river. Bugis merchants at Samarinda handle most of its trade.

nations.name: Selangor
nations.eraSummary: Selangor's Bugis sultans hold the coast between Perak and the Linggi river. Tin is mined up the Klang and Selangor rivers on a small scale.

nations.name: Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach
nations.eraSummary: Grand Duke Karl Friedrich succeeded his father Karl August in 1828. Weimar had the first constitution in the German Confederation in 1816, and Goethe still lives in the town.

nations.name: Bima
nations.eraSummary: The sultan of Bima rules eastern Sumbawa under a Dutch contract. The island has not recovered from the Tambora eruption of 1815.

nations.name: Sukadana
nations.eraSummary: Sukadana is a small sultanate on the southwest coast of Borneo. The Dutch have taken an interest in reviving its port.

nations.name: Parma
nations.flagNote: existing game design in the yellow and blue of the ducal arms
nations.eraSummary: Marie Louise of Austria, Napoleon's widow, holds Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla for life under the 1815 settlement. Austrian advisers run the duchy, and it will return to the Bourbons after her.

nations.name: Negeri Sembilan
nations.eraSummary: Negeri Sembilan is a federation of Minangkabau chiefdoms under the Yang di-Pertuan Besar at Seri Menanti. The local chiefs, chosen by matrilineal custom, hold most of the power.

nations.name: Bali
nations.eraSummary: Bali is divided among Hindu rajas who acknowledge the Dewa Agung of Klungkung as first among them. The island sells slaves and rice to Batavia and the Straits.

nations.name: Montenegro
nations.eraSummary: The aged Prince-Bishop Petar I governs the Montenegrin clans from Cetinje. The mountains have not acknowledged Ottoman authority for a generation.

nations.name: Oldenburg
nations.eraSummary: Paul Friedrich August succeeded as ruler in 1829 and took the title of Grand Duke. Oldenburg has no constitution and also holds the exclaves of Lubeck and Birkenfeld.

nations.name: Nassau
nations.eraSummary: Duke Wilhelm rules from Wiesbaden under the constitution of 1814, the earliest in Germany. The duchy's spas and Rhine wines draw visitors from across Europe.

nations.name: Brunswick
nations.eraSummary: Duke Charles II refuses to recognise the constitution agreed during his minority and is at odds with his estates and with Hanover.

nations.name: Mecklenburg-Strelitz
nations.eraSummary: Grand Duke Georg rules from Neustrelitz under the same estates settlement as Mecklenburg-Schwerin. It is a quiet agricultural state with close ties to the British royal family.

nations.name: Saxe-Meiningen
nations.eraSummary: Duke Bernhard II gained Hildburghausen and Saalfeld in the 1826 partition of the Gotha inheritance. A new constitution for the enlarged duchy was issued in 1829.

nations.name: Sine
nations.eraSummary: The Maad a Sinig rules the Serer kingdom of Sine from Diakhao. Sine has resisted the spread of Islam and keeps the Serer religion.

nations.name: Lanao
nations.eraSummary: The Maranao principalities around Lake Lanao form a loose confederation of four districts. No sultan rules them all, and Spain has never reached the lake.

nations.name: Bone
nations.eraSummary: Bone is the leading Bugis kingdom of south Sulawesi. Dutch expeditions in 1824 and 1825 failed to subdue it.

nations.name: Mwali
nations.eraSummary: Mwali is the smallest of the Comoro sultanates and has long resisted claims by Ndzuwani to rule it.

nations.name: Lippe
nations.eraSummary: Prince Leopold II rules Lippe from Detmold. The constitution of 1819 has never come into force because the estates rejected it.

nations.name: Waldeck
nations.eraSummary: Prince Georg Heinrich rules Waldeck and Pyrmont from Arolsen under the estates constitution of 1816.

nations.name: Bahrain
nations.eraSummary: The Al Khalifa have ruled Bahrain since 1783 and signed the General Maritime Treaty of 1820. Pearling pays for the island, and Oman, Persia and the Wahhabis all claim it.

nations.name: Andorra
nations.eraSummary: Andorra is a co-principality of the Bishop of Urgell and the King of France, governed day to day by its Council of the Land.

nations.name: Ndzuwani
nations.eraSummary: Sultan Abdallah II rules Ndzuwani from Mutsamudu, which supplies ships on the route to India and claims overlordship of Mwali.

nations.name: Bremen
nations.eraSummary: The Free Hanseatic City of Bremen is governed by its senate and merchant burghers. In 1827 it founded Bremerhaven on land bought from Hanover to keep its port open to large ships.

nations.name: Maldives
nations.eraSummary: The sultan rules the atolls from Male and sends tribute to Ceylon. Cowries, coir and dried fish are traded to India.

nations.name: San Marino
nations.eraSummary: The republic is governed by its Grand and General Council and two Captains Regent. Napoleon left it independent, and the Congress of Vienna confirmed it.

nations.name: Hamburg
nations.eraSummary: The Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg governs itself through its senate and burgher assemblies, a member of the German Confederation and the busiest port in the German lands.

nations.name: Free City of Kraków
nations.eraSummary: Created at the Congress of Vienna, the Free City of Kraków is a small republic under the joint protection of Austria, Prussia and Russia, the last free fragment of the old Polish state.

nations.name: Frankfurt
nations.eraSummary: The Free City of Frankfurt hosts the Federal Diet of the German Confederation and the banking houses that finance half its princes.

nations.name: Lübeck
nations.eraSummary: The Free Hanseatic City of Lübeck keeps its senate and its Baltic trade, a member of the German Confederation.

nations.name: Lucca
nations.eraSummary: The Duchy of Lucca is held by the Bourbon-Parma line until Parma itself falls to them, under the Vienna settlement.

nations.name: Anhalt
nations.eraSummary: The three Anhalt duchies of Dessau, Bernburg and Cöthen are small Ascanian states on the middle Elbe within the German Confederation.

nations.name: Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
nations.eraSummary: Duke Ernst I has just united Coburg and Gotha, a Thuringian duchy whose family is marrying into the thrones of Europe.

nations.name: Saxe-Altenburg
nations.eraSummary: Saxe-Altenburg was reconstituted in the 1826 Ernestine partition, a small Thuringian duchy of the German Confederation.

nations.name: Reuss
nations.eraSummary: The Reuss principalities of the elder and younger lines, every prince named Heinrich, sit in eastern Thuringia.

nations.name: Schwarzburg
nations.eraSummary: The two Schwarzburg principalities, Rudolstadt and Sondershausen, are small Thuringian states of the German Confederation.

nations.name: Hohenzollern
nations.eraSummary: The Catholic Swabian principalities of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen and Hechingen, cousins of the Prussian royal house.

nations.name: Coorg
nations.eraSummary: The hill kingdom of Coorg is still ruled by its own Raja in the Western Ghats; the Company annexes it in 1834.

nations.name: Kuwait
nations.eraSummary: The Al Sabah sheikhs of Kuwait trade by sea under a loose acknowledgement of Ottoman Basra.

nations.name: Liechtenstein
nations.eraSummary: The Principality of Liechtenstein is a sovereign member of the German Confederation whose princes live in Vienna.
